title: Solve static Peierls distortions and electronic structure
action: Self-consistently solve the 2D SSH model on a 64×64 square lattice at T=0 with electron‑lattice coupling λ=0.65 for two distortion patterns: pattern (a) with Fourier components Q=(π,π) and Q/2, and pattern (b) with Q, Q/4, and 3Q/4. Determine electronic eigenenergies and wavefunction coefficients for both patterns.
description: Self-consistent solution of the electronic states in the presence of multimode static lattice distortions. The outputs are used later to build the phonon dynamical matrices.

title: Construct phonon dynamical matrices
action: For each distortion pattern, construct the 2N×2N dynamical matrix K_{a,b}(q1,q2;q') with group index q'=0, using the electronic states from the static solution, following the matrix definition in the paper.
description: Building the phonon eigenvalue problem matrices that are diagonalized to obtain phonon frequencies.

title: Output phonon dispersion for pattern (a)
action: For pattern (a), diagonalize the phonon dynamical matrix at each reduced-zone wavevector q = 0, …, N/4 along (q,q). Write the sorted squared phonon frequencies ω² for each q to dispersion_pattern_a.csv.
description: CSV file containing the phonon dispersion (squared frequencies) for distortion pattern (a). The number of branches is determined by the pattern.
output_schema: header: q, omega2_0, omega2_1, ... (as many columns as there are branches, sorted ascending). q is an integer representing q*N/(2π). omega2_i are floats.

title: Output phonon dispersion for pattern (b)
action: For pattern (b), diagonalize the phonon dynamical matrix at each reduced-zone wavevector q = 0, …, N/8 along (q,q). Write the sorted squared phonon frequencies ω² for each q to dispersion_pattern_b.csv.
description: CSV file containing the phonon dispersion (squared frequencies) for distortion pattern (b). The number of branches is determined by the pattern.
output_schema: header: q, omega2_0, omega2_1, ... (as many columns as there are branches, sorted ascending). q is an integer representing q*N/(2π). omega2_i are floats.
